full_text_en:
The People's Procuratorate of Guangzhou City, Guangdong Province v. Xu Xiaochun — embezzlement case

Defendant: Xu Xiaochun, male, 33 years old, formerly the contractor of the business department of Guangdong Kanghui Trade Development Company, arrested on July 15, 1992.

The People's Procuratorate of Guangzhou City, Guangdong Province instituted a public prosecution with the Guangzhou Intermediate People's Court against the defendant Xu Xiaochun for embezzlement.

The Guangzhou Intermediate People's Court found through open trial: In October 1989, the defendant Xu Xiaochun colluded with Wang Shuyi, an accountant at the Huayuan Business Office of the Guangzhou Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China, to engage in embezzlement. Wang Shuyi, taking advantage of her position, provided Xu Xiaochun with the monthly report of large deposits of the business office. Xu Xiaochun selected from it the Guangzhou Qiaofeng Trade Service Department and the Business Department of Guangdong Electronic Technology Import and Export Company as the units to be impersonated for issuing drafts, and, based on photocopies of the seal cards of the above two units that Wang Shuyi had retained at the Huayuan Business Office, forged the special checks seals and the seals of the responsible persons of the above two units, and further forged a bank draft entrustment letter for a remittance of RMB 3,000,000 from the Guangzhou Qiaofeng Trade Service Department and a bank draft entrustment letter for a remittance of RMB 500,000 from the Business Department of Guangdong Electronic Technology Import and Export Company. On November 17 of the same year, Wang Shuyi inserted these two forged draft entrustment letters into the normal work procedures of the Huayuan Business Office, passed the seal verification review by deception, and issued two formal drafts to Xu Xiaochun, and sent a telegram to notify the receiving bank, the First Business Office of the Zhuhai Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China. Xu Xiaochun used the two formal drafts to transfer RMB 3,500,000 to the account of the Zhuhai Wanshan Management Zone Border Small Trade Company at the receiving bank. Thereafter, with the help of others, Xu Xiaochun transferred the sum to Hong Kong, converting it into HKD 4,549,997.86, which was deposited by his agent in Hong Kong into a bank account opened there. Xu Xiaochun and Wang Shuyi successively fled to Hong Kong, and on December 27 of the same year, they fled to Taiwan with the stolen funds to hide. In June 1990, Xu Xiaochun was arrested by the Taiwan police. In December 1991, Xu Xiaochun was repatriated and surrendered; Wang Shuyi remains at large. After the case was uncovered, none of the stolen funds could be recovered.

The above facts are confirmed by documentary evidence such as the two forged bank draft entrustment letters by Xu Xiaochun, the forensic science identification report of the Guangzhou Public Security Bureau, and witness testimony, and Xu Xiaochun also confessed to the facts.

The Guangzhou Intermediate People's Court held: Although the defendant Xu Xiaochun was not a bank employee and did not take advantage of his own official position, Xu Xiaochun, in collusion with a bank employee, used the means of forging draft entrustment letters to misappropriate and take away the huge deposits of bank customers. In accordance with Article 1, Paragraph 2 of the Supplementary Provisions of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on the Punishment of Embezzlement and Bribery, Xu Xiaochun, in collusion with a state functionary, jointly committed embezzlement and is an accomplice in embezzlement. Even though the bank employee Wang Shuyi has not yet been brought to justice, the existing evidence in this case is sufficient to confirm this criminal fact. The amount of embezzlement by Xu Xiaochun is particularly huge, causing significant economic losses to the state, and the circumstances of the crime are particularly serious. He shall be severely punished in accordance with Article 2, Paragraph 1, Item (1) of the Supplementary Provisions. Xu Xiaochun shall also be deprived of political rights for life in accordance with Article 53, Paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China. Accordingly, the court rendered the following judgment on July 27, 1993:

The defendant Xu Xiaochun is guilty of embezzlement and is sentenced to death, and deprived of political rights for life.

The defendant Xu Xiaochun, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, filed an appeal on the ground that he did not collude with Wang Shuyi in committing the crime, but rather personally forged the draft entrustment letters to defraud the bank of RMB 3,500,000, and that his act should be characterized as fraud.

The Guangdong High People's Court upon trial held: After his arrest, the appellant Xu Xiaochun repeatedly confessed to having committed the crime through internal and external collusion with the bank employee Wang Shuyi. In his confession, Xu Xiaochun stated that he selected the two units that could be impersonated for issuing drafts from the business office's monthly report of large deposits provided by Wang Shuyi, that Wang Shuyi inserted his two forged draft entrustment letters into the normal work procedures of the business office, and that, taking advantage of the busy time of the seal verification staff, she substituted for them in verifying the seals on the forged draft entrustment letters, allowing the forged draft entrustment letters to pass through. These details in Xu Xiaochun's confession are corroborated by documentary evidence and witness testimony. Wang Shuyi was responsible for compiling statistics on large deposits at the business office and had comprehensive knowledge of the names, fund flow, and account balances of large deposit customers. Only one copy of the monthly large deposit report was produced each month, and that report was also kept by Wang Shuyi. Without Wang Shuyi taking advantage of her position and conspiring with Xu Xiaochun, Xu Xiaochun could not have accurately selected customers with slow fund flow and large account balances to impersonate as the units issuing drafts, nor could he have accurately defrauded the bank of RMB 3,500,000 by means of forged drafts. Therefore, even though Wang Shuyi is a fugitive, the evidence in this case is sufficient to establish that Wang Shuyi took advantage of her official position to jointly commit embezzlement with Xu Xiaochun; no other person, including other staff members of the business office, had the means to commit the crime. Xu Xiaochun's denial of joint commission with Wang Shuyi and his claim that he acted alone and did not take advantage of any official position, and thus his act should be characterized as fraud, are not only uncorroborated by witness testimony, documentary evidence, and other evidence, but also objectively no such conditions for committing the crime existed. Therefore, this ground of appeal is a mere argument advanced to evade the severe punishment provided by law for his joint embezzlement and shall be rejected. The first-instance trial had clear factual findings, conclusive evidence, correct characterization of the crime, appropriate sentencing, and lawful trial procedures. Accordingly, the Guangdong High People's Court, in accordance with Article 136, Item (1) of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, ruled on August 17, 1993, to reject the appeal of Xu Xiaochun and affirm the original judgment, and, in accordance with Article 144 of the Criminal Procedure Law, submitted the case to the Supreme People's Court for approval.

The Supreme People's Court reviewed this case and ruled on September 7, 1993, to approve the criminal ruling of the Guangdong High People's Court upholding the Guangzhou Intermediate People's Court's judgment that the defendant Xu Xiaochun committed embezzlement and was sentenced to death and deprived of political rights for life.
